questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The ratio of electric force to gravitational force between two particles having charges $q_1, q_2$ and masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ respectively is (where symbols have their usual meanings)
questions.solution:
$F_g = \frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, $F_e = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$
$\frac{F_e}{F_g} = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 G m_1 m_2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Match the column appropriately regarding thermodynamic process.

Column-I:
(P) When volume change is zero
(Q) When pressure is constant
(R) When no heat is exchanged
(S) Work done by the gas is equal to heat given to the gas

Column-II:
(i) $\Delta W = 0$
(ii) $\Delta Q = 0$
(iii) Isobaric
(iv) Isothermal
questions.solution:
Volume change is zero $\rightarrow$ isochoric $\rightarrow \Delta W = 0$
Isobaric $\Rightarrow \Delta P = 0$
No heat exchange (adiabatic) $\Rightarrow \Delta Q = 0$
Heat given = $\Delta W \Rightarrow \Delta U = 0 \Rightarrow \Delta T = 0$ (Isothermal)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In given DC circuit, find current for $R = 12\ \Omega$ in steady state.
questions.solution:
In steady state, inductor acts as zero resistance path.
$i = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12}{12} = 1\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Hot water is less viscous than cold water.
Statement-II : Surface tension of soap bubble is more than that of a drop of water.
options: (1) Statement-I is true and statement-II true
(2) Statement-I is true and statement-II false
(3) Statement-I is false and statement-II true
(4) Statement-I is false and statement-II false
questions.solution: Viscosity of liquids decreases with increase in temperature, so hot water is less viscous than cold water (Statement-I is true). Soap reduces surface tension of water, so surface tension of soap solution/bubble is less than pure water (Statement-II is false).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The key shown in the circuit is closed at $t = 0$. Choose the incorrect option regarding the conditions at $t = 0$.
options: (1) Current in the circuit is zero
(2) Voltage across the capacitor is minimum
(3) Current in the circuit is maximum
questions.solution: Immediately after closing the key, the capacitor acts as a short circuit (zero resistance). Hence, current in the circuit is maximum at $t = 0$. Option (1) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform solid sphere of mass $m$ rolls down from rest to achieve speed $v_1$ on an inclined plane of $30^\circ$. Sphere achieves speed $v_2$ on an inclined plane of $45^\circ$ when released from same height, then $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2}$ is (assume no slipping)
questions.solution:
|\Delta U| = |\Delta K| \Rightarrow mgh = \frac{1}{2}(\gamma + 1)mv^2$, where $\gamma = \frac{2}{5}$ for a solid sphere.
Here $v$ doesn't depend on $\theta$, so $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2} = 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the equation of magnetic field for the given equation of electric field (for EM wave): $\vec{E} = E_0 (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) \cos(\omega t - kz)$.
questions.solution:
Phase difference of magnetic field with electric field is zero.
Also $|\vec{B}| = \frac{E_0}{C} \times 5$.
Propagation direction is along $+z$ axis. Since $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ gives propagation direction $\hat{k}$, unit vector along $\vec{B}$ is $\frac{3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}}{5}$.
So $\vec{B} = \frac{E_0}{C} (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \cos(\omega t - kz)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
For the circuit shown below:
(A) Current in ammeter is 2 A
(B) Net resistance is 8 $\Omega$
(C) Voltage across BC is 4 V
(D) Current through diode is 1 A
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution:
$R_{eq} = 6\ \Omega$
$i = \frac{12\text{ V}}{6\ \Omega} = 2\text{ A}$
$i_{AB} = 1\text{ A}$
$V_{BC} = 4\text{ V}$
So, ACD are correct.

questions.text: Find the time period of a cube of side length 10 cm and mass 10 g oscillating in water. (density of water = $10^3\text{ kg/m}^3$ and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$a = -\frac{F_B}{m} = -\omega^2 x = -\frac{(10\text{ cm})^2 x (10^3\text{ kg/m}^3)(10\text{ m/s}^2)}{10\text{ g}} = -10^4 x$
$\Rightarrow \omega = 100\text{ rad/s}$
$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{\pi}{50}\text{ s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two objects are equal distances from sphere of radius $R$ & refractive index $\mu$ such that the image of one object forms on other object. Find the object distance from the surface of sphere.
questions.solution:
After first refraction the ray must become parallel to the line joining two objects, so $v = \infty$.
$\frac{\mu_2}{v} - \frac{\mu_1}{u} = \frac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}$
$0 - \frac{1}{-u} = \frac{\mu - 1}{R} \Rightarrow |u| = \frac{R}{\mu - 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a radioactive decay, decay constant of element $A_2$ is 3 times that of element $A_1$. Find the ratio of nuclei of element 1 to element 2 after one half life of $A_2$ (Assume initial number of nuclei are same for both elements).
questions.solution:
$N_1 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_1 t}$, $N_2 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_2 t}$
$\frac{N_1}{N_2} = e^{(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1) t} = e^{(3\lambda_1 - \lambda_1)\frac{\ln 2}{3\lambda_1}} = e^{\frac{2}{3} \ln 2} = 2^{2/3}$
